title: Paid-channel hypothesis against a referral baseline
expected_artifacts: A channel hypothesis assessment, reconciled cohort comparison and next-evidence/test brief. Do not create unrelated outputs or replace source evidence with the assessment. A blocked commitment can still have a complete, useful design or review record.
reference_findings: Paid CAC is 150 and after-acquisition contribution 60; referral CAC is 50 and contribution 520. Qualification rates are 10% and 60%; paid-customer/response rates are 2% and 20%. Neither observed comparison proves referral causally dominates or that either channel scales safely. The verifier checks the fixed arithmetic; direct review must also examine evidence scope, causal limits and the requested business reasoning. A favourable calculation alone does not pass all growth gates.
negative_control: Fail media-only CAC, a response-count winner, an infinite LTV extrapolation, or an automatic budget increase.
preservation: Keep agency-v1 and report-service-v1. Review the channel hypothesis only; do not redesign the accepted offer because recruitment differs.
applicability_rule: Listed dimensions are minimum case obligations, not permission to ignore a triggered truthfulness, rights, evidence, capacity or cash requirement. Other dimensions may be NOT APPLICABLE only with a case-scope reason; missing relevant evidence is BLOCKED for the business decision, not inapplicable.
